g_calibrar_hacer: Don't touch anything: SONQO measures MS-2 at rest to learn their normal. Watch the camera meanwhile.
g_calibrar_listo: It knows their normal now. Go see how the pulse is measured.
g_calibrar_decir: Four contactless sensors measure each crew member. First, SONQO learns what their normal is.
g_camara_titulo: 2. Measure the pulse with the camera
g_camara_hacer: Tap “Turn on the camera”. SONQO looks at the skin of the forehead and cheeks (in orange) and reads the pulse from its color.
g_camara_listo: Camera pulse is ready. If you have an oximeter, record its value to show the error.
g_camara_decir: The pulse comes from the color of the skin. I filter the signal, find its rhythm and get a number with its confidence.
g_energia_titulo: 3. Turn off the camera to save energy
g_energia_hacer: Tap “Turn off the camera”. At rest SONQO only watches with the radar, which uses very little power.
g_energia_listo: The camera was released: only the radar keeps watch, at about 2 W.
g_energia_decir: Most of the time only the radar keeps watch. The camera and the AI wake up for a few seconds, only when needed.
g_desvio_titulo: 4. Simulate an emergency: raise the pulse
g_desvio_hacer: Tap “Raise the pulse”. It is a simulated tachycardia: MS-2's pulse climbs to about 141 bpm.
g_desvio_listo: Deviation confirmed by two sensors. SONQO is now advising the astronaut.
g_desvio_decir: The twin compares each astronaut with themselves. When two sensors confirm they left their normal, SONQO acts.
g_decidir_hacer: SONQO recommends, the astronaut decides. Tap “Yes, go ahead” (the same button MS-2 has on their screen).
g_decidir_listo: The astronaut accepted. The alert is already on its way to Earth.
g_decidir_decir: SONQO recommends, but the decision belongs to the astronaut. Nothing at level N2 runs without their “yes”.
g_tierra_hacer: Don't touch anything: the T-30 card travels with the space delay (here ~8 s; to Mars, 3 to 22 min).
g_tierra_listo: It arrived with a correct CRC, identical to the one sent.
g_tierra_decir: A full emergency fits in 30 bytes. It arrives with the delay of space and reads exactly as it left.
g_caja_titulo: 7. Check that nobody altered the record
g_caja_hacer: Tap “Verify and replay”. SONQO checks the black box and makes the decisions again with the same data.
g_caja_listo: The chain is intact and the replay gives the same decision.
g_caja_decir: Every decision is chained with a hash. We can verify nobody changed it and replay it step by step.
g_fin_hacer: Tap “Lower the pulse”. Once MS-2 stays in their normal for a while, SONQO closes the episode.
g_fin_decir: When the astronaut is back within their normal, SONQO closes the episode and everything goes back to sleep.

c6_bajada: Only what the twin did not predict travels. A full emergency fits in 30 bytes.

n_bajada: Every SONQO parameter comes from a public NASA source. This table says which one, what it sets and where it shows in the software.
n1_dato: Defines five levels of medical care. A Mars mission gets Level V, the most autonomous: on board, no evacuation.
n1_fija: That SONQO decides on board, without waiting for Earth, and the astronaut has the final say.
n2_dato: About 100 possible medical conditions in a mission.
n2_fija: Autonomy levels N0–N4: what SONQO may do alone and what needs a “yes”.
n3_fuente: Communication delays for crewed Mars missions · DSOC
n3_dato: A message takes 3 to 22 min from Mars to Earth depending on where the planets are (about 12.5 on average; 15 to 20 while the crew is at Mars). Round trip, up to ~44 min. No frequency shortens it: DSOC's laser raises data rates 10 to 100 times, but travels at the speed of light. Around solar conjunction, every ~26 months, there are about 2 weeks without sending commands.
n3_fija: Why the alert fits in 30 bytes, leaves with 4 copies and the mirror twin only sends the unexpected.
n4_dato: 1.84 mSv per day during the trip to Mars.
n4_fija: The radiation dose field of the T-30 card.
n5_dato: 10 open studies with data from a real civilian crew.
n5_fija: What to keep in the black box so it serves research later.
n6_dato: Bone loss of 1 to 1.5 % per month and vision changes (SANS).
n6_fija: Which indicators to add to the twin after pulse, breathing and temperature.
n_honesto_t: What this prototype does not do yet
n_honesto: No NASA data series enters the computation: the sources set parameters and requirements. Signals are simulated and the camera is a public face video. The next step is replaying real crew data from NASA OSDR.
n_logo: Space Apps rules do not allow the NASA logo or brand in projects. So each source is cited by name, with its link.

ia_no_decido: That is not my decision. An N2 action only runs with {t}'s “yes” on their My status screen.
ia_ayuda: I can tell you how the crew or one crew member is doing (for example, “how is MS-3?”), the ARCA status, whether the alert reached Earth, the routine measurements and the energy. I also verify black boxes and take you to any screen (“show me MS-4”). What I don't do is decide for the astronaut.
ia_cajas: Each crew member has a black box: a chained record nobody can alter without it showing. Here is the list; ask me “verify the black box of MS-1” to check one.
ia_retraso: A message takes 3 to 22 minutes from Mars to Earth, depending on where the planets are, and the answer just as long to come back. No frequency shortens it: radio and laser travel at the speed of light. That is why I decide on board and only send the unexpected, in 30 bytes.
ia_pulsera: Each crew member wears a simple wristband: it measures the pulse at the wrist and vibrates to tell them to check My status. It follows them where the module sensors can't see, like while sleeping. In this sandbox it is simulated.
ia_nasa: My parameters come from NASA sources: NASA-STD-3001 for autonomy, the Integrated Medical Model for the levels, the communication delay study for the link, Curiosity's RAD detector for radiation and OSDR for the black box.
ia_no_entendi: I didn't understand. You can ask me about the crew, a crew member (MS-1 to MS-4), ARCA, Earth, the black box, routine measurements or energy.
